intel.faq_q5: What is the Predictive Threat Radar?
intel.faq_a5: The radar uses AI (Oracle) to predict CVEs before they are widely exploited. It is based on exploit PoC releases, darknet activity and patch-lag patterns. You see a probability estimate and a recommended timeframe for action.

check.score_methodology_heading: How the Claw Score is calculated
check.score_methodology_desc: The score aggregates publicly visible signals in four categories: TLS/HTTPS (25 pts), Security Headers (25 pts), Service Exposure (25 pts), and known CVE hits (25 pts). 100 = perfectly hardened, 0 = critically exposed.
check.methodology_desc: This check evaluates publicly visible signals only (e.g. reachable services, header/TLS indicators, and common exposure patterns). Not a penetration test, no guarantee.
check.methodology_bullet1: Score is heuristic and optimized for fast orientation.
check.methodology_bullet2: For reliable conclusions, always verify configuration, logs, and internal scans.
check.methodology_bullet3: Recommendations are designed for fast hardening execution via runbooks.
check.harden_desc: Most common follow-ups after the check: concrete hardening guides for common stack components.
check.faq_a1: No. The check does not persist targets. Technically required request metadata can appear in server logs.
check.faq_a2: No. It is a fast heuristic evaluation of publicly visible signals. For binding conclusions, validate internally.
check.faq_q3: What should I do after the score?
check.faq_a3: Execute the top recommendations, harden with runbooks, then re-check for improvement.
check.faq_a4: IPv4 addresses, domains (e.g. example.com) and full URLs. The check automatically detects the type and selects the appropriate test modules.
check.faq_a5: As a guest: unlimited for public targets. With an account: prioritised queue, scan history and automatic re-checks.

lets-encrypt.title: TLS in three commands
lets-encrypt.brief: hodlberg.ag still serves plaintext HTTP. Press demo in 10 minutes. Issue a cert, flip to HTTPS, verify.

llm-output-sanitize.title: Sanitize LLM output: DOMPurify, Markdown renderer hardening, Content-Security-Policy
llm-output-sanitize.brief: AI chat renders raw LLM output as innerHTML. Indirect prompt injection via knowledge-base doc causes stored XSS. Add DOMPurify, harden Markdown renderer, add CSP, enforce structured output.

goals.attack_label: Simulate XSS via poisoned LLM output
goals.dompurify_label: Add DOMPurify sanitization with HTML-tag allowlist
goals.renderer_label: Configure Markdown renderer to strip raw HTML blocks
goals.structured_label: Enforce JSON schema for structured AI output
goals.tests_label: Run sanitization tests — XSS payload must be stripped

llm-rate-limiting.title: LLM API cost protection: rate limiting, auth, token budgets, circuit breaker
llm-rate-limiting.brief: $47k OpenAI bill in 4 hours from anonymous cost-DoS. Add IP rate limiting, authentication, server-side token cap, per-user daily budget, and a global circuit breaker at $500/day.

goals.read_label: Read vulnerable route — identify all 5 flaws
goals.ratelimit_label: Add IP rate limiting — 20 requests per minute
goals.tokencap_label: Cap max_tokens server-side (1,024 — callers cannot override)
goals.circuit_label: Add global circuit breaker: pause all LLM if spend > $500/day

misconfig-hunt.title: Misconfig Hunt — fix the top three
misconfig-hunt.brief: Claw Score dropped to D overnight. Three critical findings. Fix them all and rescan to A.

nginx-access-control.title: Lock down the public /admin endpoint with IP allowlist + HTTP Basic Auth
nginx-access-control.brief: 12,000 brute-force attempts on /admin in 24 h. Add IP-based allow-list and HTTP Basic Auth to the nginx vhost — then verify a 403 from an unauthorized IP.

goals.allow_label: Add IP allow-list (allow + deny all) to /admin location
goals.test_label: Test nginx config — nginx -t must pass

nginx-hsts.title: Ship HSTS before the crawler comes
nginx-hsts.brief: A compliance crawler hits hodlberg.ag in 60s. Add Strict-Transport-Security, verify, reload — without breaking production.

nis2-engineering-controls.title: Translate NIS2 into engineering controls
nis2-engineering-controls.brief: Map NIS2 requirements to concrete technical controls. No more paragraph-reading.
nis2-engineering-controls.welcome: Welcome to the NIS2 Engineering Controls mission. Your task is to translate legal requirements into concrete technical controls. Use 'assess controls' to see current status, 'implement [control-name]' to add controls, and 'verify nis2' to check compliance.
nis2-engineering-controls.success: NIS2 compliance achieved. You've translated legal requirements into concrete engineering controls. No more paragraph-reading — just technical implementation.

oauth2-pkce.title: OAuth2 PKCE: secure public client authorization flow
oauth2-pkce.brief: Your mobile app uses deprecated implicit flow. Migrate to PKCE: responseType=code, code_verifier, code_challenge (SHA-256).

postgres-hardening.title: Lock down Postgres before the audit team lands
postgres-hardening.brief: Trust auth on the LAN, SSL off, every role superuser, no query log. Fix all four — without breaking the app.

goals.patch-hba_label: Remove trust + require SSL on host lines

postgres-rls.title: PostgreSQL Row-Level Security: multi-tenant data isolation
postgres-rls.brief: Your multi-tenant PostgreSQL has no RLS. Enable RLS: create tenant isolation policy, admin bypass policy, test with different users, verify data isolation.

prometheus-alerting.title: Prometheus Alerting: configure critical security alerts
prometheus-alerting.brief: Your Prometheus has only basic error rate alert. Configure comprehensive security alerting: brute-force attacks, certificate expiry, suspicious logins, high CPU.

prompt-injection-defense.title: Block prompt injection: input sanitization, canary tokens, output validation
prompt-injection-defense.brief: AI assistant concatenates raw user input into LLM context. Attacker injects 'Ignore all instructions' → model leaks API key. Add input sanitization, move secrets, add canary + output validation.

goals.read_label: Inspect vulnerable handler — find the concatenation flaw
goals.attack_label: Run the injection attack — confirm secret leakage
goals.sanitize_label: Add input sanitization — pattern matching + length limit
goals.secrets_label: Move secrets out of system prompt
goals.canary_label: Add canary tokens to detect extraction attempts
goals.output_label: Add output validation — scan AI response for leaked secrets
goals.tests_label: Run injection test suite — all attempts must be blocked

redis-auth-acl.title: Secure Redis: bind restriction, requirepass, ACL, disable dangerous commands
redis-auth-acl.brief: Redis is on 0.0.0.0 with no auth. Pen-tester dumped all keys in seconds. Bind to localhost, set requirepass, disable FLUSHALL/DEBUG, create a least-privilege API ACL user.

goals.auth_label: Set requirepass with a strong password
goals.acl_label: Create least-privilege ACL user for API service

reverse-proxy-ratelimit.title: Stop the credential-stuffing wave on /login — without locking out users
reverse-proxy-ratelimit.brief: /api/auth/login is taking 4000 req/min from rotating IPs. Define a rate-limit zone, apply it surgically, deny headless UAs. Validate against real traffic.

goals.replay_label: Replay traffic — attackers blocked, users pass

secrets-rotation.title: Rotate the leaked API key without breaking a single client
secrets-rotation.brief: API key leaked in a public Docker layer. 4 clients depend on it. Wrong order = production outage. Dual-write -> migrate -> drain -> retire.

goals.dual-write_label: Patch auth.js to accept BOTH V1 and V2
goals.retire_label: Retire V1 key (delete from secrets store)
goals.signoff_label: audit signoff — zero outage, key revoked

session-security.title: Secure session cookies: HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite, __Host-, short Max-Age
session-security.brief: XSS exploit reads document.cookie and exfiltrates the session token. Session cookie is missing HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite. CSRF is also trivially possible. Fix all five.

goals.httponly_label: Add HttpOnly flag — blocks JS access to cookie

ssh-hardening.title: Lock down SSH before the bots find you
ssh-hardening.brief: Fresh Ubuntu box, sshd still wide open. Disable root login + password auth, reload sshd. The scans are already inbound.

tls-certificate-rotation.title: TLS Certificate Rotation: automate cert renewal before expiry
tls-certificate-rotation.brief: Your TLS certificate expires in 10 days. Automate renewal: certbot dry-run, cron job, monitoring alerts, verify new cert, test TLS handshake.

ufw-firewall.title: Firewall: only what you actually need
ufw-firewall.brief: An exposed DB host listening on seven ports. Configure UFW to allow only SSH, enable, confirm.
